gen-gf-unlock-fs-paquito: Loud and measured: Unlock's little entry notches mark every round letter. Paquito, a confident serif whose caps barely rise above its lowercase, settles in beneath, a good match for a quick look rather than a marathon.
gen-gf-victor-mono-fs-ranade: Chalk-on-slate spacing and bold, uniform strokes give Victor Mono a precise, technical edge. Ranade, a sans-serif with sturdy hairlines and a slight stretch in its weight, loosens things up below.
gen-gf-victor-mono-montserrat: Wide-spaced, technical and bold: that is Victor Mono at a glance. Victor Mono does precision best, while Montserrat, the sans-serif body, glides along on oversized e and a counters.
gen-gf-walter-turncoat-fs-karma: Loose, marker-weight handwriting with a tall middle band: that's Walter Turncoat. Karma, the classic serif, brings a soft cadence of fuller stems and slimmer links that the heading's flat marker line lacks.
gen-gf-warnes-fs-ranade: Ranade reads with a slight, rubbery shift in weight and stroke ends set far apart, a comfortable midpoint between flat and dramatic strokes. Warnes, with no contrast to slow the eye, keeps pages moving.
gen-gf-zen-maru-gothic-fs-literata: Modern and unfussy, Zen Maru Gothic leaves its curves open. Literata, bookish and sophisticated, adds a restrained step from stem to connecting stroke, which sits comfortably under that heading.
gen-indie-flower-fs-amulya: Amulya reads contemporary and modern, its curves left generously open. Indie Flower brings hand-drawn charm at its best in a line or two, and leaves the steady work to the sans-serif body.
gen-indie-flower-fs-literata: Relaxed and hand-drawn, Indie Flower looks like cord cut into letters. Literata, bookish and sturdy, takes over once text runs on, since the handwritten heading wouldn't hold up across paragraphs.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-syriac-eas: Noto Sans Syriac Eastern keeps a tall lowercase and curve endings well apart. Irish Grover, the display heading, shares that height and adds open throats and softly varied strokes for a fun, organic feel.
gen-luckiest-guy-fs-ranade: Luckiest Guy is loud and cheerful, with a high mean line and a single-weight outline feel. Ranade, a sans-serif whose curves thin out modestly, gives it somewhere quieter to land.
